intro: Dear colleagues, here are the geotechnical stories from around the world that caught our eye last week. We gather them from news sources in different languages, and the ISSMGE Magazine Presidential Committee (MPC) checks every issue before it is published.

highlights.text: What ground and geological risks must a privately developed subsea rail tunnel address under the Gulf of Finland?
What site investigation methods are needed to characterise seabed soils across large offshore wind zones under a multiyear framework?
Why did the concrete arch dam survive a rockslide-generated wave overtopping it, and what does this teach about reservoir slope hazards and dam design?
What are the challenges of marine geotechnical site investigation for a first offshore wind project, from seabed sampling to geophysical interpretation in unfamiliar ground?
How can a tunnel be enlarged in situ while keeping the surrounding rock and lining stable, and what ground risks does this method carry?
